CRITICAL (1)
  * aws_sqs_queue.work["orders"] and aws_sqs_queue.work["order_events"] share an identity across a destroy/create pair: possible address rename [PLAN-RENAME-001]
    aws_sqs_queue.work["orders"] will be destroyed because its for_each key changed, and aws_sqs_queue.work["order_events"] will be created with the same name ("fixture-lifecycle-orders"). A shared identity suggests a possible address rename; it does not establish that these are the same cloud object. The SQS queue would be destroyed with it, losing every message still in the queue.
    -> Confirm that both entries refer to the same provider configuration, account, region and cloud object before considering a moved block (from = aws_sqs_queue.work["orders"], to = aws_sqs_queue.work["order_events"]). Otherwise review the intended migration and any uniqueness constraints on name.

MEDIUM (1)
  * aws_iam_role.deploy will be destroyed and recreated [PLAN-REPLACE-001]
    The IAM role is replaced because name ("fixture-lifecycle-deploy-v1" → "fixture-lifecycle-deploy-v2") cannot be changed in place. The new object is created before the old one is destroyed (create_before_destroy).
    -> Check that the identifiers other systems hold for this resource (ARN, ID, DNS name, IP) are not referenced outside Terraform, or plan a cutover.

    The SQS queue's policy comes from a value the plan cannot show (a data source, a template or an attribute of another resource).
